title: Batched complete-hand on-policy collector
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Batched inference and retaining hero observations eliminate redundant forward replay while preserving sampled trajectories within floating point tolerance.
material_change: Isolated complete-chronology batched CPU collector, actual shifted commitment targets, two retained seed Adam updates.
notes: Preregister64 batch plus64 serial same-deal hands per seed1/3; exact action and terminal parity, sampled log probability tolerance2e-4, finite real update. Performance fixture, not strength gate. GPU not tested in this run.

result.summary: Batched collector passed both64-deal seed fixtures, exact serial action/payoff parity and finite retained Adam updates;181.6 and257.5 CPU collection hands/sec.
result.conclusion: Batch timings .352/.249s versus serial1.844/1.656s: approximately5.2x/6.7x faster collection on small fixtures. Maximum log-probability differences6.2e-6/1.5e-5 below2e-4. Timings exclude optimizer, evidence IO and model loading; not production throughput or strength.128 serial executions deliberately reuse batch decks.
result.decision: Use batched retained-observation collection for the bounded on-policy trial, keeping execution contract explicit.
result.next_step: Add durable source-bound update transactions and matched namespaces to the online runner; qualify clean resume and fail-closed crash tails, then run two-seed controlled learning doses.
